question.prompt:
A circle of radius \(1\) is surrounded by \(4\) circles of radius \(r\) as shown. What is \(r?\)

[Figure 1](figures/2007_AMC_10B_Q18_question_fig1.svg)

solutions.explanation:
Joining the circle centers turns each external tangency into a distance equal to the sum of two radii.

[Figure 1](figures/2007_AMC_10B_Q18_question_fig1.svg)

Let \(O\) be the center of the unit circle, and label the four outer centers \(P,Q,R,S\) in order around it. Since the outer circles have positive radius \(r\), their depicted tangencies give
\[
OP=OQ=OR=OS=r+1
\]
and
\[
PQ=QR=RS=SP=2r.
\]
The four triangles \(OPQ\), \(OQR\), \(ORS\), and \(OSP\) are congruent by side-side-side: each has side lengths \(r+1,r+1,2r\). Their angles at \(O\) fill a complete turn, so each is \(360^\circ/4=90^\circ\). This establishes the right angle needed for the Pythagorean theorem without assuming that the centers form a square from appearance alone.

In right triangle \(OPQ\), the legs have length \(r+1\) and the hypotenuse has length \(2r\). Hence
\[
2(r+1)^2=(2r)^2.
\]
Because \(r>0\), taking positive square roots gives \(r+1=\sqrt{2}\,r\). Therefore
\[
r=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}-1}
=\frac{\sqrt{2}+1}{2-1}
=\boxed{1+\sqrt{2}}.
\]
The denominator \(\sqrt{2}-1\) is positive, so this is the unique positive solution. The answer is choice \(\boxed{\text{B}}\).
solutions.title: Join the circle centers
